reason: E1 supports the general oxygen storage and redox properties of CeO2, but none of the cited evidence demonstrates in-situ formation of CeO2 nano-domains within a multi-element nearly equiatomic alloy, nor does it show that such domains protect against H2O/NO/aging deactivation or improve durability without extra PGM. E2 and E3 are about different dopants (Mg, Bi, Pd) and different catalyst systems, providing no direct support for the key premises.
premises: CeO2 provides oxygen storage and redox buffering via Ce3+/Ce4+ cycle and oxygen vacancies
CeO2 nano-domains can be formed in-situ during synthesis of a multi-element alloy
Oxygen vacancies from CeO2 protect active sites from deactivation by H2O, NO, and thermal aging
CeO2 addition improves catalytic activity and durability without increasing PGM consumption
The benefits apply under low-temperature, transient exhaust conditions with H2O and NO
